title: 1.2.28 September 2, 1843
book: The First Fifty Years of Relief Society
notes: 119 primary documents; Church Historians Press; EN-only

footnotes.text: On the Snow house, see 113n256 herein.

This minute book numbers Relief Society meetings in sequence for each of the three years it covers. For 1843, the minutes have no record for the ninth meeting, which would have been a meeting of the Fourth Ward Relief Society. As noted here, what would have been the ninth meeting was evidently canceled because of bad weather.
text:It appears that the scribe accidentally noted this amount as six dollars, then corrected the amount to six cents. The scribe made a similar mistake on the next line.
A mantuamaker is a dressmaker. “Mantua,” a corrupted form of the French “manteau,” is a lady’s gown. (“Mantua,” and “Mantuamaker,” inAmerican Dictionary[1845], 516.)
